answer:
The case uses the interFoam solver (VOF, transient, two-phase) to model gravity-driven sloshing in a stationary rectangular tank.
The simulation is 2D: the tank spans 1.0 m in x (from 0 to 1), 0.6 m in y (from 0 to 0.6), and 0.1 m in z.
Build the mesh with blockMesh using a single block of 200 cells in x, 120 cells in y, and 1 cell in z, and apply the empty boundary type to both the front patch (z = 0) and the back patch (z = 0.1) so the case runs as a 2D simulation.
Set gravity in constant/g to (0 -9.81 0) m/s² for the full run.
Initialize the velocity field U to (0 0 0) everywhere.
Initialize alpha.water with a linearly tilted free surface such that the water depth is 0.25 m at x = 0 and 0.35 m at x = 1, i.e. the free surface lies on the line y = 0.25 + 0.10·x and water fills the region below it, giving a mean depth of about 0.30 m so the tank is effectively half-full.
Apply this tilted initial condition by starting from a uniform alpha.water = 0 field and using setFieldsDict to set alpha.water = 1 in every cell whose centre lies below the line y = 0.25 + 0.10·x.
Set the top patch (y = 0.6) to open-atmosphere boundary conditions: pressureInletOutletVelocity for U, totalPressure with p0 = 0 for p_rgh, and inletOutlet with inletValue = 0 for alpha.water.
Set the left wall (x = 0), right wall (x = 1), and bottom (y = 0) to no-slip solid walls: noSlip for U, fixedFluxPressure for p_rgh, and zeroGradient for alpha.water.
Run the case for endTime = 10 s, which captures 7 to 8 natural sloshing periods before viscous damping noticeably decays the oscillation.
Use adaptive time stepping with adjustTimeStep yes, maxCo = 0.5, maxAlphaCo = 0.5, an initial deltaT = 1e-3 s, and a safety cap of maxDeltaT = 1 s.
Write results every 0.05 s using writeControl adjustableRunTime and writeInterval 0.05, with purgeWrite = 0 so every snapshot is retained.
Set writeFormat to binary, writePrecision to 6, timeFormat to general, timePrecision to 6, and runTimeModifiable to yes in controlDict.
Define two incompressible Newtonian phases in constant/transportProperties: water with nu = 1e-6 m²/s and rho = 1000 kg/m³, and air with nu = 1.48e-5 m²/s and rho = 1 kg/m³.
Set the surface tension coefficient sigma to 0.07 N/m between water and air in transportProperties.
Run the case as laminar in constant/turbulenceProperties with simulationType laminar, so all damping of the sloshing motion comes from molecular viscosity at the no-slip walls and within the fluid.
Use the standard interFoam numerical schemes in system/fvSchemes, with vanLeer for div(phi,alpha) and div(phirb,alpha), Gauss linearUpwind for div(phi,U), and Gauss linear corrected for laplacian terms, and use the standard interFoam linear solver settings in system/fvSolution (PCG/GAMG for p_rgh with tolerance 1e-7, smoothSolver for U with tolerance 1e-8) so the VOF interface stays sharp and the free-surface oscillation is well resolved.
